The boundary confines every connected new originalWrite
$$C_i=[a_i+2,a_{i+1}-1]_{\mathbb Z}\times[1,W]_{\mathbb Z}.$$
Its one-step exterior boundary is occupied by retained endpoints:Row  $a_i+1$ , columns  $1,\ldots,W$ , is the complete inner row of  $B_i$ , including the two stem junctions.Row  $a_{i+1}$ , columns  $1,\ldots,W$ , is the outer row of  $B_{i+1}$ .Columns  $0,W+1$ , throughout the relevant row interval, belong to the continuous walls of  $A$ .The depth assumptions supply these wall points and the corners. The old short stems inside  $C_i$  are additional blockers; their presence cannot create an exit.Let  $T$  be a connected new endpoint set disjoint from all old endpoints. If  $T$  contains both an endpoint in  $C_i$  and one outside it, take a nearest-neighbour path between them within  $T$ . The first vertex outside  $C_i$  lies on its occupied boundary. That contradicts endpoint disjointness. Hence
$$T\cap C_i\ne\varnothing
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
T\subseteq C_i.$$
This proof has no source-dimension cutoff. It uses connectivity of the induced nearest-neighbour endpoint graph, which the canonical full U and rotor records possess. For a U, the bar joins both continuous stems; for the rotor, the central four-cycle joins all four terminals.Therefore every new original belongs to exactly one chamber class or to the exterior class. This applies equally to selected and unselected originals.2. Tile parity gives genuine exterior separationConnectivity alone would not establish the required accounting separation. $$Q_i=
\left[
\frac{a_i}{2}+1,\frac{a_{i+1}}2-1
\right]_{\mathbb Z}
\times
[0,W/2]_{\mathbb Z}.$$
More explicitly, their union of cells is
$$\bigcup_{\tau\in Q_i}\tau
=
[a_i+2,a_{i+1}-1]_{\mathbb Z}
\times[0,W+1]_{\mathbb Z}.$$
The equality depends on all three parity conditions:the first interior row  $a_i+2$  is even;the last interior row  $a_{i+1}-1$  is odd; $W$  is even.Thus a chamber tile contains no cell beyond the top or bottom boundary. Its only cells outside  $C_i$  are on the occupied sidewalls  $0,W+1$ .It follows that any new endpoint in a tile of  $Q_i$  is inside  $C_i$ . Its entire owner consequently belongs to  $Y_i$ . An exterior new original cannot share even one physical tile with a chamber new original.The  $Q_i$  also have disjoint tile-row intervals for distinct gaps. Therefore:
$$\operatorname{tiles}(T(Y_i))
\cap

=\varnothing

These are the precise footprint separations needed for the mixed-tile and intratile-event identity.A useful distinction from the earlier selected-owner theorem is that an unselected owner may reach row  $a_i+2$ . The present chamber definition includes that row. The new N family does reach it when  $b=10$ , and its tile footprint still satisfies the required separation.3. The inherited support conditions are localThis part requires a fact about the canonical records in addition to endpoint connectivity: every original support point is adjacent to an endpoint of its own original. That fact follows directly from the supplied definitions.For a U, the bar-end, terminal and alternating side supports each neighbour the corresponding bar or stem endpoint. For the rotor, the eight supports pair with its four terminals as follows:Canonical supportsAdjacent canonical terminal $(0,2),(1,1)$  $(1,2)$  $(2,5),(1,4)$  $(2,4)$  $(5,3),(4,4)$  $(4,3)$  $(3,0),(4,1)$  $(3,1)$ Every allowed transformation preserves this adjacency.Now let  $S$  be the occupied endpoint union of an actual complete extension, and let  $Y_i$  contain all its new originals in chamber  $C_i$ . Put
$$S_i=T(O)\cup T(Y_i).$$
For every  $x\in C_i$ , its occupied status is the same in  $S$  and  $S_i$ . Moreover,
$$\mathcal N(x)\cap S=\mathcal N(x)\cap S_i,$$
where  $\mathcal N(x)$  is its four-neighbour set. Indeed, any neighbour outside  $C_i$  is on the already occupied old boundary, while every new endpoint inside belongs to  $Y_i$ .Consequently, an unconsumed support  $x\in C_i$  satisfies
$$|\mathcal N(x)\cap S_i|
=
|\mathcal N(x)\cap S|
=1.$$
There are no hidden exterior support obligations inside the chamber:A support of a chamber source lying outside  $C_i$  must be on the old boundary, because it neighbours that source’s endpoint. It is already consumed.An exterior new source cannot have a support inside  $C_i$ . Its adjacent own endpoint would then have to be either inside  $C_i$ , contrary to its class, or on the occupied old boundary, contrary to endpoint disjointness.This proves the claimed inherited local conditions.
